differential_reading.note: Both windows' identical-code controls skew the same way (window1 2x8192 +3.31% favor P; window2 3x6144 +4.19% favor P). Change-domain shapes in the same windows skew favor C. Control-bias-corrected separation in window2 is ~7-8pp on 1x32768/2x16384/8x16384. Raw deltas are therefore conservative under a P-favoring measurement bias. This is an analytical reading, not the protocol's formal noise-band test.

local_verdict_reason: MAIN-1 rule: direction-consistent but still inside the noise band -> maintain. Direction is now statistically established (24/31 pairs, p=0.0017; 4/4 window-2 change-domain shapes negative medians) and mechanism amplitude matches prediction in window 2. However the stated goal (compress same-code band below +/-1.5%) was NOT achieved: short-kernel controls still show half-width 3-5% with tails to +19%, and raw change-domain medians (-0.67% to -3.86%) sit inside that band. Only 8x16384 exceeds its own same-binary noise scale (2.53%). Keep Candidate, do not stack changes.
decision_package_for_main: Option A (formal): one more window with a tighter control set (change-domain shapes themselves as their own same-binary reference; or protocol-approved REPEAT_BATCH_N calibration after same-binary validation) to push the band below the effect size.

Option B (differential): accept on differential grounds — controls skew +3-4% favor P in both windows while change-domain skews favor C in the same runs; bias-corrected effect is ~-7.7pp with amplitude match. If Main accepts this reading, LOCAL_ACCEPTED is defensible now.
